chapter: Steamer Capitol and New Orleans bands
title: The Desvigne band, and drummers Judge Raleigh and Ransom Nolan
summary: He recalls bandmates in Desvigne's band and two New Orleans musicians now living in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Yes, very much so. But I left New Orleans on the steamer capital in 1936 I think it was, yes.

Yes, he was leader of the band, that, ever since band then. And I worked with fellows like, well, Judge Raleigh, I don't know whether you know him or not, but incidentally he's in Chicago too. Judge Raleigh, he is a drummer.

That's right. Charlie Elgar gave me his name a long time ago when we were, Natty Dominic was playing some dances. Oh, is that right? And we needed a drummer because Baby Dodds wasn't so well, wasn't able to play the whole dance, so we had two drummers.
Yeah, well I wish I had known him. I could have gotten contact for you. Jasper Taylor, but Raleigh is from New Orleans. Judge Raleigh.

Next time I'm here I'll try to get to talk to him. I never met him. He used to be a fine drummer too. Is he fairly young or old or something? Well, I think he's about my age. He might be a year or two older than I am, but not very much more than that. Then there's another fellow in Chicago too from New Orleans, his name is Ransom Nolan. But he wasn't, I don't think he was born in New Orleans, but he had moved to New Orleans at an early age and he stayed around there. And he worked with several of the bands around New Orleans. Of course I could remember some very fine units that had come from the old style groups, come from fellas that had taught younger fellas like the fellas that worked with A.J. Peerron. I don't know whether you remember A.J.
